rules.title: Respect module boundaries
rules.text: Respect module boundaries; depend on public interfaces, not internals of other modules.

rules.title: Small focused functions
rules.text: Keep functions small and single-purpose; extract when a function mixes levels of abstraction.

rules.title: Avoid premature abstraction
rules.text: Prefer a little duplication over a premature abstraction; abstract after the third repetition.

rules.title: Separate pure logic from I/O
rules.text: Keep business logic pure and push I/O to the edges so it is easy to test.

rules.title: Prefer immutability
rules.text: Prefer immutable data and avoid mutating function arguments.

rules.title: Remove dead code
rules.text: Delete unused code and commented-out code instead of leaving it behind.

rules.title: Record decisions
rules.text: Record significant architectural decisions in docs/adr before implementing them.

rules.title: Inward dependencies
rules.text: Keep dependencies pointing inward: domain code must not import framework or infrastructure code.

rules.title: Composition over inheritance
rules.text: Prefer composition and small interfaces over deep inheritance trees.

rules.title: Single source of truth
rules.text: Keep one source of truth for each piece of data and derive the rest.

rules.title: Build only what is needed
rules.text: Implement only what the task requires; no speculative options or extension points.

rules.title: Group by feature
rules.text: Group code by feature or domain rather than by technical type when the project already does so.

rules.title: Small public surface
rules.text: Export the minimum from each module and keep helpers private.

rules.title: Idempotent background jobs
rules.text: Write background jobs so they can be retried or run twice safely.

rules.title: Prefer boring solutions
rules.text: Prefer proven simple solutions over clever or novel ones.
